years.name: The Opportunity
headlines: Rates stay low as startup filings hit a record.
Aurelia named 'best city to launch' for the second year.
Co-working vacancies near zero in Startup Hub.
Online retail spending up 14% year-on-year.

years.name: Growth Fever
headlines: Aurelia rents up 10% as the startup boom fills every desk.
Hiring gets harder: wages up 8% in a year.
Everyone is raising a round. Not everyone should be.

years.name: Supply Shock
headlines: Port of Aurelia backed up for a third week: 40 ships waiting.
Container rates double. Couriers add fuel surcharges.
Retailers warn of empty shelves before the holidays.
PostPoint hiring: parcel volumes at a record.

years.name: The Green Shift
headlines: Clean Packaging Act passes: $0.40 levy on plastic-padded parcels.
City opens a $2M Green Business Grant for local sellers.
Solar desk lamps are this year's must-have gift.
Verdant Supply opens a warehouse in the Industrial Zone.

years.name: Clearing Crisis
headlines: Cross-border payments stuck: correspondent banks slow down checks.
Importers report wires taking 5 to 9 days to clear.
Banks push letters of credit; fintechs push 'digital dollars'.
Regulators: 'Know who you are paying, and how.'

years.name: Digital Finance Boom
headlines: Digital-dollar payments double as fintechs race to win importers.
Nexus Bank pilots escrow on delivery with a payments start-up.
Wires recover: cross-border payments now clear in 3 to 5 days.
Import prices ease as the ports catch up.

years.name: Bridge Exploit
headlines: Digital dollars now settle one in four cross-border invoices.
Bridge volumes hit a record: $2 billion moved in a month.
Analysts: 'Faster rails, thinner buffers.'
Import lead times settle at two weeks.
headlines_incident: BRIDGE EXPLOIT: attackers drain the reserve behind the digital-dollar rail.
Operators freeze all bridge transfers for about a week while they trace the funds.
Banks: wires and letters of credit are unaffected.
Operators: 'Most balances will be restored. There is a shortfall.'
headlines_after: Bridge reopens with new limits; operators restore 90 cents on the dollar.
Importers go back to wires and letters of credit for big orders.
Payments start-ups promise audits and an insurance pool.
Regulators call hearings: 'Who holds your money in between?'

years.name: Regulation Wave
headlines: Payments Integrity Act takes effect: know-your-customer checks on transfers over $2,500.
Commercial importers now need a licence: City Hall opens a new permits counter.
Compliance officers are this year's hottest hire.
Big firms are buying small ones to absorb the paperwork.

years.name: Global Consolidation
headlines: Regional marketplaces open to Aurelia exporters; local-currency prices required.
Nexus Bank opens international accounts for registered companies.
Customs warns: buyers may refuse parcels with unexpected arrival duties.
